Object construction and validity in energyRt

Source: R/class-validity.R
energyRt-validity.Rd

The package states one rule for how its S4 objects come into being and what they guarantee once they exist. The rule is the contract the rest of the package is written against, and it has three parts.

Constructors are the supported path

Every class has a public constructor – newCommodity(), newTechnology(), newStorage(), newModel() and so on. The constructors are the only route through the construction checks: column names are validated against the class, types are coerced, renamed columns are diagnosed, and conflicting rows are detected. An object returned by a constructor is a complete, documented object of its class, and methods::validObject() accepts it.

Direct new() refuses slot values

new("<class>", slot = value) raises an error naming the constructor to use instead. The passthrough initialize() methods these classes define would otherwise discard the value in silence – a technology asked for by name came back named "" – and assigning the slot directly would skip every check listed above. new("<class>") with no arguments remains supported and returns the class prototype.

Two generated classes are deliberate exceptions and still assign named arguments to slots, because newParameter() and the internal model-data machinery are built on that behaviour: parameter and variable.

Prototypes are drafts, not public objects

A prototype obtained from a bare new("<class>") is an internal starting point. It is not required to satisfy validObject(), and one does not: a prototype scenario carries empty model, settings, modInp and modOut slots, because building valid empties for them costs time that would be paid on every package load for an object no user asks for. newScenario() returns a valid scenario; new("scenario") is a draft that the interpolation and solve pipelines fill in.

Everything a user is handed – by a constructor, by interpolate(), by a solve – is a valid object of its class. Validity of a bare prototype is not promised, and code that needs the guarantee should construct through the constructor rather than validate a prototype.

See also

newModel(), newScenario(), newTechnology()
